title: Treat workbooks as a first-class artifact family
decision: Archivist should treat workbooks as a first-class artifact family. Appendix A / HVA is the first concrete workbook implementation, not a one-off special case.
context: The EPP corpus currently contains one true assessment workbook, Appendix A, but the user expects future document sets to include other workbook-style artifacts. The imported EPP artifact inventory also contains adjacent structured tools such as calculators, logs, directories, forms, inventories, quizzes, and charts.
rationale: A workbook needs more than document rendering: it has a structured definition, guided workflow, user-entered state, derived outputs, review/export behavior, and history expectations. Treating HVA as a one-off would make future workbooks harder to add and would blur the boundary between document text and interactive local tool state.
alternatives_considered: Implement Appendix A as a custom HVA-only component
Treat every artifact renderer as the same kind of embedded document widget
Convert workbook data into ordinary Markdown sections
consequences: Archivist needs a reusable workbook contract before the HVA prototype is considered complete
Workbook definitions can be document-bound while workbook state remains structured and auditable
HVA should validate the workbook class with scoring, mitigation actions, review evidence, JSON import/export, and print output
Other artifact families can remain separate from workbooks when they do not need multi-step state, derived summaries, or review/export packets
